answer: We commit 744,000 accepted units of FL-2280 to Anselm Precision Components for the 2026 plan year, 31 release lots of 24,000.

driver: The forward rate is a property of whether each unit's commitment fence covers the supply lead time, a classification built by comparing two files and filed nowhere, and because two large units moved to a shorter fence at renewal, every rate carried forward from the closed years, pooled or per unit, overstates the commitment.
driver_concrete: Programmes whose schedule freezes at or before the 11-week cumulative lead time call off 95.9% of plan and the rest 52.3%; FP-1205 and FP-1533 republished on a shorter fence for 2026, so the group rates give 749,926 units, 31 lots of 24,000 (744,000), against 840,000 per programme and 864,000 pooled.
stump: Measures each programme's own call-off rate over the five closed plan years, carries it onto the 2026 plan and commits 840,000 units (35 lots), because only the 2026 rows of the schedule revision file show FP-1205 and FP-1533 republished on a shorter fence at renewal.
